question: How many people did you support or have living with you, not counting your spouse?
why_ask: Each possible dependent is checked separately.
retrieval_query: dependents qualifying child qualifying relative tests

question: Did they live with you for more than half of last year?
why_ask: A qualifying child must live with you more than half the year (with some exceptions).
retrieval_query: residency test qualifying child more than half the year
origin: IRS Direct File flow (TY2024), adapted; Form 13614-C (Rev. 10-2025) Part II

question: Is any of them your child (or stepchild, foster child, sibling, or their descendant) under 17 at the end of the year?
why_ask: A qualifying child under 17 may qualify for the Child Tax Credit.
retrieval_query: child tax credit qualifying child under age 17

question: Is any child under 6 at the end of the year?
why_ask: California's Young Child Tax Credit applies to a child under 6 when the family qualifies for CalEITC.
retrieval_query: California young child tax credit CalEITC

question: Do you support anyone else, such as a parent or other relative, who is not your child?
why_ask: A qualifying relative may be claimed if you pay more than half of their support.
retrieval_query: qualifying relative support test gross income test

question: Is any of them a full-time student aged 19 to 23, or permanently disabled?
why_ask: Students under 24 and disabled people of any age can still be qualifying children.
retrieval_query: qualifying child age test student permanently disabled

question: Do you share custody of a child with a parent who does not live with you?
why_ask: Children of divorced or separated parents have special rules on who may claim them.
retrieval_query: children of divorced or separated parents custodial parent Form 8332

question: Could anyone else, such as the other parent or a grandparent, also claim any of these people?
why_ask: When more than one person could claim a child, tie-breaker rules decide.
retrieval_query: tiebreaker rules qualifying child of more than one person

question: Did you pay someone to care for a child under 13 or a dependent who can't care for themselves so you could work or look for work?
why_ask: Work-related care costs may qualify for the Child and Dependent Care Credit.
retrieval_query: child and dependent care credit work-related expenses
origin: IRS Direct File flow (TY2024), adapted; Form 13614-C (Rev. 10-2025) Part IV

question: Did any of that care include after-school programs or summer day camps?
why_ask: After-school care and day camps can count as care; overnight camps do not.
retrieval_query: day camp overnight camp child care credit

question: Do you have each care provider's name, address and tax ID (or Social Security number)?
why_ask: The credit requires the provider's identifying information.
required_docs: provider name, address and tax ID

question: Did your employer give you dependent care benefits (shown in box 10 of your W-2)?
why_ask: Employer dependent care benefits reduce the expenses that count for the credit.
retrieval_query: dependent care benefits W-2 box 10 Form 2441

question: Did a nanny or other caregiver work in your home, paid by you?
why_ask: Paying a household employee can create employment tax duties.
